title: Applying imaging flow cytometry and immunofluorescence in studying the dynamic Golgi structure in cultured cells
protocol: Seed 2–4 × 10^5 HeLa cells per well in a 12-well culture dish containing one 18 mm diameter sterile microscope cover slip and complete medium in each well for immunofluorescence (IF).
Seed 5 × 10^5 HeLa cells in a 60 mm plate in complete medium for immunostaining (ISX).
Place the seeded cells at 37°C humidified atmosphere with 95% air and 5% CO2 incubator.
Allow the cells to attach for approximately 18–20 hours.
Block mitotic progression by adding nocodazole directly into the complete medium at a final concentration of 0.3 μM.
Incubate for 16 hours.
Treat cells with thymidine by adding it to a final concentration of 2 mM into the complete medium.
Incubate for 16 hours.
Aspirate complete medium containing thymidine and rinse plates twice with PBS.
Add complete medium for 8 hours.
Repeat thymidine treatment for an additional cycle of 16 hours.
Wash plates twice with PBS after second thymidine block.
Apply fresh complete medium to mark time 0.
Aspirate complete medium from each well carefully.
Wash cells once with PBS to remove residual medium.
Aspirate PBS immediately.
Fix cells with 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS, 1 mL per well.
Incubate fixed cells for 20 minutes at room temperature (22–25°C).
Remove PFA and add PBS for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Repeat wash with PBS three times to remove residual PFA.
Permeabilize cells with Triton X-100.
Block cells with bovine serum albumin (BSA) by applying 1 mL of blocking-permeabilization solution per well.
Incubate permeabilized and blocked cells for 5 minutes at 23°C.
Optional: Permeabilize cells with 0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS, 5 minutes at 23°C.
Optional: Block cells with 2% BSA in PBS, 15 minutes at 23°C.
Prepare the primary antibody solution by diluting the GM130 antibody at a ratio of 1:100 in PBS for a total volume of 25 μL per sample.
Remove the blocking solution and wash cells once with PBS.
Apply a drop of 25 μL diluted antibody on parafilm for each slide.
Invert each cover slip onto the liquid drop containing the antibody dilution to ensure the cells are facing the antibody.
Cover the parafilm with an aluminum foil covered box and attach wet Kimwipes on top to maintain humidity.
Incubate the slides for 1 hour at room temperature (RT).
Transfer coverslips back to a 12-well plate and wash cells three times with PBS, each for 5 minutes at RT.
Dilute Alexa Fluor 568 conjugated antibody 1:400 in PBS.
Dilute DAPI for nuclear staining at a dilution of 1:250 in PBS.
Mix the diluted secondary antibody with DAPI.
Apply a drop of 25 μL diluted secondary antibody on parafilm for each slide.
Invert coverslips onto the secondary antibody drop and incubate for 1 hour (at RT) using a humidified covered box.
Transfer coverslips back to the 12 wells tissue culture plate.
Wash cells with PBS three times to remove residual antibody.
Prepare microscope slides marked with specific cell type, treatment, and antibody wavelength.
Apply a drop of 10-20 μL Elvanol mounting solution per coverslip.
Invert each slide slowly on the mounting reagent.
Place cells side facing down within an angle until fully placed.
Carefully place the slides in a covered dark place.
Allow slides to dry overnight at room temperature.
Transfer slides from the well plate to the paraffin back and forth optionally.
Apply primary or secondary antibody mix directly into coverslips in the well plate as an alternative.
Image by spinning disk confocal microscopy.
Analyze images.
Turn on the Observer.Z1 Confocal Spinning Disk Microscope and ZEN 2.5 system software.
Add DAPI channel with 405 nm laser and BP450/50 emission filter.
Add AF568 channel with 532/561 nm excitation and 529/62 emission filter.
Optimize image settings to avoid saturation for each channel while maximizing dynamic range of the camera.
Capture images using a 63×/1.4 NA oil immersion objective according to specific microscope software.
Capture images from at least five different fields on each slide.
Ensure a total capture of at least 100 cells per treatment for quantification.
Acquire more images if cell confluency is low to ensure statistical significance.
Transfer acquired images to Photoshop software (only for viewing).
Maintain original scientific information in the transferred image.
Analyze and quantify fine Golgi structure according to GM130 staining manually for each cell within each frame.
Identify intact Golgi as one concentrated GM130 spot (∼2–3 μm) adjacent to the nucleus.
Recognize initial fragmentation as a more spread (>4 μM), less intense GM130 staining.
Determine partial fragmentation by observing 2–5 distinct spots of GM130 staining.
Identify fully fragmented Golgi as diffused GM130 staining throughout cells.
Consider using automated programs for microscope data analysis such as Image J, ilastik, or CellProfiler.
Use automated programs together for better quantification when combined.
Manual counting is preferred due to the fluidity and variability of Golgi structure among cells.
Count cells in each field and document the number of cells with fragmented Golgi.
Document the number of cells with intact Golgi.
Repeat counting in 5 different fields for a total of at least 100 cells.
Calculate the percentage of cells containing fragmented vs. intact Golgi out of the total cells counted.
Determine significance using Student’s T-test to determine differences between untreated and mitosis-induced cells.
Collect the complete medium from each 60 mm culture dish.
Transfer the collected medium into a 15 mL conical centrifuge tube.
Place the tube on ice.
Prepare additional plates for single-color controls and unstained samples.
Wash culture dishes with PBS.
Aspirate the PBS from each dish and add 500 μL of Trypsin C solution.
Incubate the dishes in a 37°C incubator for 3–5 minutes to detach cells.
Use the medium from step 26 to wash detached cells.
Collect the washed cells and return them to the tube.
Spin down the cell suspension at room temperature (RT) for 5 minutes at 300 × g.
Aspirate the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 5 mL of ice-cold PBS.
Centrifuge again at RT for 5 minutes at 300 × g to remove residuals.
Aspirate the supernatant and resuspend the cell pellet in 500 μL of ice-cold PBS.
Set vortex conditions to a low mixing level.
Gently vortex the cell suspension while slowly adding 1.7 mL of ice-cold methanol drop by drop.
Place the samples at 4°C for an overnight incubation.
Add 6 mL of ice-cold PBS (at 4°C) to each tube and spin down at RT for 5 minutes at 300 × g.
Repeat the washing process once more to remove all residual methanol.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 500 μL of 0.1% Triton X-100 and 2% BSA in PBS.
Incubate for 5 minutes at 23°C.
Wash cells by adding 6 mL ice-cold PBS.
Spin down at room temperature for 5 minutes at 300 × g.
Prepare the primary antibody solution by diluting GM130 antibody at a ratio of 1:100 in PBS, for a total volume of 100 μL per sample.
Aspirate the supernatant and resuspend the cell pellet in 100 μL primary antibody dilution.
Mix on an orbital mixer for 1 hour at 4°C.
Wash cells by adding 6 mL ice-cold PBS.
Spin down at room temperature for 5 minutes at 300 × g.
Prepare the secondary antibody solution containing Alexa Fluor 568 conjugated antibody (1:400) and DAPI (1:250) in PBS.
Aspirate the supernatant in the tube and resuspend the cell pellet in 100 μL secondary antibody solution.
Mix on an orbital mixer for 30–60 minutes at 4°C.
Wash cells by adding 6 mL ice-cold PBS.
Spin down at room temperature for 5 minutes at 300 × g.
Aspirate the supernatant in the tube and resuspend the cell pellet in 200 μL PBS.
Turn on the imaging flow cytometer.
Log in to the acquisition computer.
Start the acquisition software, INSPIRE (version 200.1.681.0).
Click on ‘STARTUP’ in the software.
Ensure all automatic calibrations and tests have passed (marked green).
Choose the magnification according to cell size.
Set the excitation/emission data for dyes.
Turn on relevant lasers.
Set lasers to maximal power.
Use the 561 nm laser (200 mW) for AF568 dye.
Use the 405 nm laser (120 mW) for DAPI.
Turn on the relevant acquisition channels for your dyes.
Load your first sample – start with the sample that contains all dyes, which is expected to produce the highest staining intensity.
Create a scatter plot of the Area vs. Aspect ratio of the bright-field channel.
Create a histogram of Gradient_RMS of the bright-field channel.
Draw a linear gate that includes values between 55 and 90 to collect only cells in focus.
Create a ‘Raw Max Pixel’ histogram for each fluorescent channel taken from the ‘single’ gate.
Reduce laser intensity if values reach 4095, preferably less than 4000.
Collect approximately 30,000 cells from each sample using the same setup of lasers and acquisition channels as set in step 47.
Adjust cell position manually on the ‘Centering’ tab if not centralized.
Disable autofocus by going to Instrument-> Advanced settings-> Autofocus and disabling the option.
Acquire single stained controls with the compensation wizard using the same laser settings as for experimental samples.
Set analysis template in IDEAS software version 6.2 or higher.
Open control experimental sample file and calculate compensation using single-stain files acquired with compensation wizard in IDEAS.
Draw a bi-variate plot of Area vs. Aspect ratio of the bright-field channel.
Gate around the single cells population, usually with low area and high aspect ratio.
Verify gate by visual inspection of cells.
Include telophase cells for cell-cycle analysis if required (close-to-doublet population with higher area and lower aspect ratio).
Draw a bi-variate plot of RMS vs. Contrast of the bright-field image.
Gate on focused cells, usually values higher than 55 for Gradient RMS and higher contrast values.
Verify gate by visual inspection of cells.
Draw a bi-variate plot of Area vs. Centroid X of the bright-field channel.
Gate on uncropped cells, which have already higher values of Centroid X.
Draw a bi-variate plot of Intensity vs. Max Pixel values of the Golgi staining channel.
Gate on cells with positive Golgi staining (Golgi +) by comparing to control samples labeled with all dyes except Golgi staining.
Define populations: Manually select a group of cells with an intact Golgi using ‘Tag Objects’.
Select another group featuring a fragmented Golgi using ‘Tag Objects’.
Include around 100 cells per group.
Define masks: Calculate several masks that delineate the Golgi staining.
Use the ‘Morphology’ and ‘Threshold’ masks, and recommend using several ‘Threshold’ values.
Calculate all features using the ‘Add Multiple Features’ option in the ‘Features’ panel.
Select all feature options under the ‘Size’, ‘Location’, ‘Shape’ and ‘Texture’ categories.
Choose the Golgi staining channel under ‘Image’.
Click on ‘Add Features’ to add selected features.
Discriminating statistics: Add a new statistics table.
Under ‘Statistics’, choose ‘RD-Mean’ and ‘RD-Median’.
Choose the intact Golgi cells as the reference population.
Click on ‘Add’ to calculate.
Copy the values obtained to an Excel file.
Arrange the values in descending order according to the RD values.
Examine the ability of features with the highest RD values to separate between chosen populations.
Plot histograms / bi-variate plots of selected features for visual inspection.
Apply the selected features to the whole population.
Verify that the features correspond to different Golgi morphologies.
Save the analysis template.
Open files recorded from treated samples using the saved template.
Merge treated and control samples into one file.
Click on Tools -> Create Data File from Populations in each file.
Select the single, focused, uncropped, Golgi-positive population.
Create a *.CIF file for selected populations.
Click on ‘Merge CIF files’ and select the created files.
Use the saved template to merge files.
Determine gating that distinguishes between different populations according to controls.
Verify by visual inspection of populations.
Apply the determined gating to all experimental datasets.
Apply the gating either in the merged file or save the template for other samples.
Label DNA using a dye compatible with the ones used to stain samples.
Plot DNA intensity as a histogram on a linear scale.
Determine stages of cell division by analyzing DNA morphology.
Gate for G2/M stage based on DNA staining intensity.
Gate for G2, prophase, prometaphase, and mitotic populations using bright detail intensity (BDI) of DNA staining and area of 50% highest intensity pixels.
Gate for metaphase cells according to their lower width using the Width feature masked for the 50% top intensity pixels of the DNA staining.
Define cells with higher area and lower aspect ratio in Brightfield images as belonging to the telophase stage.
Gated cells can be further classified into three populations: high Spot Area Min and 0 Spot Distance Min are considered metaphase, added to previously gated cells.
Intermediate Spot Area Min and high Spot Distance Min define anaphase cells.
Low Spot Area Min and low Spot Distance Min define Pro/ProM cells, added to previously gated cells.
